coverage_gaps: Layer 1B evidence provided in the prompt is heavily weighted toward HBM, advanced packaging, and semiconductor test/inspection; optical, power, cooling, grid, and construction candidates need fresh filing-backed validation.
Current market-cap, analyst-coverage, ownership, liquidity, short-interest, and valuation checks are still required before moving candidates into a ranked investable research list.
Several data-center electrical and cooling candidates are retained as hypotheses because segment-level AI/data-center revenue, backlog, and customer evidence were not provided in the cached context.

The universe still needs non-U.S. supplier coverage across Taiwan, Japan, Korea, Europe, and selected A-share/HK names, especially in substrates, chemicals, precision parts, probe cards, optical components, and power equipment.
Need to separate direct AI demand from cyclical recovery in telecom, semicap, industrial HVAC, electrical distribution, utilities, and construction services.

Need a systematic falsification pass for AI infrastructure overbuild, lower model compute intensity, hyperscaler capex cuts, customer dual-sourcing, rapid supply additions, grid interconnection delays, and regulatory/permitting constraints.

memory_update.text: AI should be tracked as a physical-compute, advanced-packaging, power, cooling, networking, and grid-capacity buildout rather than only a model, software, or GPU theme.
HBM and advanced-packaging test/inspection remains the best-evidenced Layer 1 chokepoint lane, with Camtek, FormFactor, Onto, Cohu, and Kulicke & Soffa requiring deeper validation.
Data-center electrical, cooling, construction, and distributed-power names should remain in the universe as underfollowed hypotheses, but require segment-level evidence before promotion.
The merged universe needs current market-cap, valuation, analyst-count, liquidity, backlog, customer-concentration, and segment-revenue screens before Layer 2 scoring.

Non-U.S. supplier coverage is insufficient; next pass should add Taiwan, Japan, Korea, Europe, and selected A-share/HK suppliers in substrates, chemicals, probe cards, optical components, precision parts, and grid equipment.

summary: Layer 1C merged the Layer 1A AI theme map and available Layer 1B node candidates into a balanced initial universe centered on physical AI compute constraints: HBM and advanced packaging, optical/networking, data-center electrical and thermal balance-of-plant, grid/power generation, semiconductor tools/materials, and second-order infrastructure/software beneficiaries. The highest Serenity relevance is assigned to companies one or two layers below the obvious AI leaders where demand linkage, qualification barriers, backlog/order signals, or capacity constraints may create chokepoints. Reference leaders are retained only as demand anchors and supplier-mapping nodes. Several names are retained as hypotheses because the hidden signal is plausible but still requires filing-backed validation.
